description: We are a curious team interested in space, technology, and software development. We aim to build an innovative solution for astronaut health monitoring. Looking for members skilled in programming, data analysis, UI/UX, aerospace, or research.
summary: ASTRA is a mission health monitoring prototype that helps astronauts, who may not be medical experts, assess their own health during long missions. Users enter heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, glucose, sleep, mood, stress and fatigue through validated forms with short measurement guidance. ASTRA compares each reading with the user's own baseline, charts trends, and flags values using explicit, documented rules, explaining the reason, the next step, and when to contact the flight surgeon. Instead of a single health score, it keeps indicators separate, distinguishes missing and stale data from normal results, and clearly labels simulated data. It is a decision-support prototype, not a medical device.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

ASTRA is a web-based health monitoring prototype for astronauts on long-duration missions, who must take more responsibility for spotting health changes themselves. Users enter heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, fasting or non-fasting glucose, sleep duration, and daily mood, stress and fatigue check-ins. Forms validate every value and reject impossible entries, explaining that the problem is the input, not the person's health. Accepted readings are stored in the browser and immediately update the dashboard, trend charts and history. Each reading is compared with the user's own earlier readings (a personal baseline, never presented as a normal range) and checked against explicit, documented rules. The Alerts page shows, for each flagged indicator, the measurement, the time, the rule that triggered, the recommended next step, and when to contact the flight surgeon or medical team. Short measurement guides explain what equipment is needed and how to measure correctly.

BENEFITS

Astronauts without medical training can see what their data means, notice changes over time, and know what to do next and when to ask for professional help. Missing and stale data are shown as such, never as "normal".

INTENDED IMPACT

To support earlier recognition of health changes during missions with delayed communication and limited medical resources, and to show how transparent, explainable rules can support (not replace) the mission medical team.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Recharts for the app structure and charts; HTML, CSS and JavaScript with SVG charts for the full ASTRA interface; browser local storage for data; GitHub for code and Vercel for hosting. No special hardware is used: measurements are entered manually. AI assistance (Claude) was used during development for coding and drafting. Health reference ranges come from public guidance (American Heart Association, CDC, American Diabetes Association, AASM/Sleep Research Society); NASA's Human Research Program informs the educational hazard content.

CREATIVITY

ASTRA deliberately avoids a single "health score". Each indicator stays separate with its own status, reason and next step. It distinguishes normal, monitor, prompt attention, uncertain, missing and stale states, uses text and symbols instead of color alone, and keeps the alert rules in one reviewable place separate from the interface.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Users are not medical experts; safety (no diagnosis, no medication advice, no false reassurance, no invented thresholds); clear labelling of simulated demo data, which is not real astronaut telemetry; privacy (data stays in the user's browser); accessibility (keyboard focus, readable contrast, mobile layout); and honesty about limits. ASTRA is a decision-support prototype, not a medical device, not clinically validated, and not an official NASA product. Some rules (self-report thresholds, freshness windows, the low-temperature limit) are prototype choices and are labelled as such. Not yet built: an interactive body map, measurement editing, device integrations and automated tests.
